medhx: Chronic kidney disease, Benign prostatic hyperplasia
notes: PSA 15 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.24. Prostate volume 64 mL. csPCa 0.87.

note_sections.t: Escalating prostate-specific antigen levels, compounded by a previously positive biopsy, drive the current clinical review.

A seventy-year-old freelance translator, initially flagged for an unexpected PSA elevation toward the end of 2022, now presents with a background of benign prostatic hyperplasia (treated with tamsulosin) and chronic kidney disease characterized by a sustained eGFR under 60 mL/min/1.73m². Though widowed, he shares a home with his partner. He abstains from tobacco, engages in biweekly tennis matches, and consumes approximately 17 units of alcohol weekly. Recent healthcare encounters outside urology encompass a vascular consultation for venous insufficiency, a standard dental inspection, and an uneventful cardiology assessment last fall. Residing well over ninety minutes from our facility, he favors remote telephone consultations when feasible.

DRE — texture: firm and homogeneous; mobility: unrestricted; asymmetry: none noted. The gland appears uniformly enlarged without discrete palpable abnormalities. Vital parameters remain stable (BP 120/68 mmHg, pulse 60 bpm). Systemic inspection yields no abnormal lymph nodes or abdominal irregularities.

admin: Lives >90 min from clinic; phone follow-up preferred where clinically safe.
